cve_summary: libndp before 1.6, as used in NetworkManager, does not properly validate the origin of Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP) messages, which allows remote attackers to conduct man-in-the-middle attacks or cause a denial of service (network connectivity disruption) by advertising a node as a router from a non-local network.
commit_message:
libndp: validate the IPv6 hop limit

None of the NDP messages should ever come from a non-local network; as
stated in RFC4861's 6.1.1 (RS), 6.1.2 (RA), 7.1.1 (NS), 7.1.2 (NA),
and 8.1. (redirect):

  - The IP Hop Limit field has a value of 255, i.e., the packet
    could not possibly have been forwarded by a router.

This fixes CVE-2016-3698.

Reported by: Julien BERNARD <julien.bernard@viagenie.ca>
Signed-off-by: Lubomir Rintel <lkundrak@v3.sk>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Pirko <jiri@mellanox.com>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Receives a message from a socket using IPv6.

Parameters: 
sockfd (int): The socket file descriptor to receive data from.
buf (void*): A pointer to the buffer where the received data will be stored.
buflen (size_t*): A pointer to a variable that holds the size of the buffer; updated with the actual size of received data.
flags (int): Flags for controlling the behavior of the receive operation.
addr (struct in6_addr*): A pointer to a structure that will hold the source address of the received message.
ifindex (uint32_t*): A pointer to a variable that will hold the interface index of the received message.
hoplimit (int*): A pointer to a variable that will hold the hop limit of the received message.

Returns: 
int: The number of bytes received, or -1 on error.

Logic: 
The function initializes necessary structures for receiving a message over an IPv6 socket, prepares to handle ancillary data, and manages the reception of the message including its address and control information.
"""
